_readme: EVERY line of text in the game lives in this file. Edit it, then re-encrypt (see README). Anything you delete falls back to the built-in copy in src/world.js.

meta.title: our little world
meta.subtitle: a tiny game about us. happy birthday ♥
intro: Mini-LA. The sun is out, the ocean is doing its thing…
…and someone with a familiar face is waiting for you by the path.
(walk with the arrow keys or WASD. press E next to sparkles, people, and cats.)

lines.text: [TODO Noah: this is 'my house' in Mini-LA — write the memory or story you want here. e.g. what you'd have shown her if she visited hometown-you.]
A walk-up window, a wall of syrup bottles, and a line that is somehow always four people long.
Brian's. shaved ice. we came here what — three times? four?
every single visit. "we're just stopping by." we were never just stopping by.
it's the best shaved ice in the county.
you say that like you've surveyed the county.
…you HAVE surveyed the county, haven't you.
(she orders the same thing every time. she has never once looked at the board.)
worth the drive. worth the line. worth the brain freeze I get every time and never learn from ♥
Low and warm and brick, with a ramp up to the doors and flowers in the boxes under every window.
your grandma's place.
I have been inside this building maybe five times and I have understood maybe eleven words of what happened in it.
she loves you.
I KNOW! that part came through fine. that part never needed translating.
go on — her room's the first on the left ♥
She's sitting up against three pillows with the TV on mute, and her hair is the exact orange it has been since before you were born.
DUSIA!!
Sashenka!! Idi syuda, idi, idi!
A! I ty tut. Nu nakonets-to! Sadis', sadis' blizhe.
she says: and there you are. finally. sit closer.
Kushal? Ty khudoi!
she asked if you've eaten. she says you're too skinny.
I ate an hour ago—
Nyet. Ne kushal.
…she's right. it was a granola bar. how does she DO that.
She takes his hand in both of hers and pats it, the way you'd pat a dog that has finally sat down.
Khoroshii malchik.
"good boy."
Sashenka. Kogda svadba?
…what. what was that one.
nothing.
SVAD-BA! Ya zhe ne vechnaya! Pravnuki! Dvoe! Tri!
she's asking when the wedding is. she says she is not eternal — and she would like great-grandchildren. two. possibly three.
tell her I'm working on it.
I'm not telling her that.
TELL HER I'M WORKING ON IT.
…on rabotayet nad etim.
Slava Bogu!!
Dusya grabs both their hands at once and doesn't let go for a while.
Khorosho. Idite gulyat'. I kushayte shto-nibud'!
we've been dismissed. and we have to go eat something.
I understood four words of that and I love her ♥
A Russian talk show, muted, in which two men in suits are furious about something.
is it always this channel?
it's always this channel.
does she ever unmute it?
never. she says she already knows what they're saying.
(from the bed, without looking over: "Tishe!" — quieter. nobody was talking.)
White walls, red stripe, and a yellow arrow you can see from three blocks away.
[TODO Noah: the In-N-Out order. Animal style? the whole thing.]
double-double, fries well done, and a twenty minute argument about the milkshake.
(the arrow points down the road like it knows something.)
Jack's house — the long low one behind all the sunflowers.
you can smell the garden from the street. tomatoes and woodsmoke.
go on, knock. nobody in there has ever knocked on anything ♥
The Pacific! It's cold and beautiful and full of surfers with better hair than Noah.
[TODO Noah: beach memory or the first-time-she-visits-LA plan.]
The tower's shutters are open and nobody's in it. Just the flag, snapping.
we sat under one of these for four hours once and didn't go in the water a single time.
A very calm horse is watching the waves. It seems to be waiting for a competition.
[TODO Noah: the Miami beach horse-competition memory — she loves riding, write it here. (riding him in-game is coming in a later update.)]
Two boards planted nose-up in the sand, still wet.
[TODO Noah: whether either of us can actually surf ♥]
A little raised bed, bursting with tomatoes. 🍅
[TODO Noah: her tomato obsession — write it here. After this, pressing E on the garden picks a tomato (they regrow).]
The pool. Perfectly still, absurdly blue, faintly smug about it.
one day we're going to argue about whether the water is 'too cold' again. I'm going to lose again.
Rows and rows of it: tomatoes up the stakes, corn taller than Jack, lettuce, peppers, herbs.
they genuinely grow most of what ends up on that table.
…we're taking some home.
(you were always taking some home.)
A ring of stones, a proper fire, three logs pulled up close.
this is the spot. this is where the night goes long and nobody notices.
[TODO Noah: the story from the fire pit ♥]
The van. Rainbow down the side, peace sign on the panel, curtains half drawn.
It has not moved in a while. It does not need to.
An old fig tree leans over the path. It smells like a Greek summer.
remember Greece? me, you, and one extremely rented quad bike.
you'd yell FIG!! out of absolutely nowhere and I'd have to emergency-brake so you could raid a stranger's tree.
FIG!!!
(you picked a perfectly ripe fig. it's yours now.)
It's THE quad bike. Somehow it followed you both home.
[TODO Noah: the Greece quad-bike memory — the drive, the dust, the backseat commentary…]
A little pond, still as glass. A couple of ducks judge you silently.
[TODO Noah: optional pond memory — or delete this point from src/maps.js if you don't want it.]
A marble column, quietly holding up the whole sky. The air smells like figs.
[TODO Noah: one line about the Greece trip.]
A pyramid! Four thousand years old and still the best-organized pile of rocks on earth.
[TODO Noah: one line about Egypt / your heritage.]
The tower leans. It has always leaned. It is doing its best.
[TODO Noah: one line about Italy — the trip or the heritage.]
A wine barrel with grapes on top — Moldova has more vineyards per person than anywhere on earth.
[TODO Noah: one line about Moldova / her roots.]
A matryoshka. Inside her is a smaller her, and inside that one, an even smaller one. Relatable.
[TODO Noah: one line about her family / heritage.]
A divi-divi tree, bent permanently southwest by wind that never stops blowing.
this one isn't a memory yet. it's a promise — next week ♥
A little easel with a map, covered in pins.
every trip we take, you can log it here — it becomes a tiny monument on this road. our world grows with us ♥
[TODO Noah: the BU building where it all started — write how you two met here.]
[TODO Noah: the first date — where it was, what you actually remember, what she claims happened instead.]
[TODO Noah: her school. Something nice about a Northeastern person, if such a thing can be written by a BU student.]
JVUE at the LMA. New brick, a lot of glass, and a little gold light over a door that has been ours for exactly eleven days.
ours.
ours. the door, the mailbox, the elevator that sighs at you.
fair warning though, it is nowhere near done. the tank's still empty. the plant shelf is still just a shelf.
…and eleven boxes.
eleven days, eleven boxes. I've decided that's a system.
I don't care. it's the prettiest place I've ever had a key to.
it's getting there. we fill it in as we go — that's honestly my favorite part.
…and there's one more thing coming for in here. not telling you yet.
(he does not elaborate. He is enjoying that far too much.)
White clapboard, wooden trim, the bottom half of a big Brookline duplex. The porch light is on.
my parents' place. bottom floor's ours — the whole thing smells like whatever mom's cooking.
they already love you. they asked about you before they asked about me.
go on. knock. …actually don't knock, just walk in, they'll be offended if you knock.
A guy in a red shirt is standing outside the brownstone like he has been waiting here specifically for you.
Mateo: "AY. You're the girlfriend. Ask me anything about this game. Anything."
…how many figs are there?
Mateo: "Twenty. I found nineteen. I do not want to talk about the twentieth one."
that's Mateo. my best friend. he playtested this whole thing for me.
and then he begged me — for two weeks — to put him in it. so. he's in it.
Mateo: "I asked ONCE."
he asked eleven times. I have the messages.
Mateo: "Worth it." (he goes back to standing there, extremely pleased.)
Past the barriers the road just… stops, and turns into white sand.
A little palapa bar stands in the sun. The board on it says CLOSED.
yeah. closed. for one more week.
then it's you, me, and an entire island. happy birthday, my love ♥
A sea turtle is sitting in the warm sand, entirely unbothered.
Turtle: "…"
Turtle: "one week."
did the turtle just—
Turtle: "see you on the beach." (he goes back to sleep.)
The Charles glitters. A sailboat drifts by, unbothered.
[TODO Noah: river walk memory — or delete this point in src/maps.js if you don't want it.]
Someone left a boombox by the river. It is, of course, playing K-pop.
…is this? IT IS.
[TODO Noah: her BTS / K-pop thing — the song, the story, the 💜. Write it proudly.]
Marina looks up from the counter and immediately starts wiping something that was already clean.
Marina!!
Marina: "So. This is the boy. Hmph. …He is taller than the photo."
(she is smiling. she will deny this.)
Your mom hugs you the way moms do — like she's checking you're all still there.
Mom: "Are you eating? You're not eating. Sit, I'll make something."
…I love it here.
Your brother is threading a line through a rod that already had a line in it.
"Hey. …Happy birthday. Don't make it weird."
"We're going out at five tomorrow. You can come. Only if you're quiet."
he scored four last weekend. FOUR. he told me twice.
(he makes it weird. he hugs you. it's very sweet.)
Leo, all seventeen pounds of orange menace, blinks at you slowly.
he's judging me.
(Leo decides he is coming too. Leo joined your little crowd! 🐱)
Charlie spins in a full circle before you even say his name.
(Charlie has decided this is the best day of his entire life.)
(Charlie joined your little crowd! 🐶)
Jack is up and across the room before you've finished shutting the door, wiping his hands on his jeans.
JACKINGTON.
Jack: "Noah! good. okay — I've got three things, and you're going to like two of them."
hi Jack—
Jack: "Hi sweetheart. so the FIRST one—"
he does this every time. I have never once made it to a chair first.
Jack: "—and if we ran a line out to the back beds the whole thing could water itself. you'd know how to do that part."
…I would know how to do that part.
and there he goes.
(they are already three steps into it. you go and find the dog.)
Dez pushes a curl out of her face with the back of a floury hand.
"Ignore him, he's been loud since he was six."
(she hands you something warm before you've said a word.)
Chakra crosses the whole room in about two steps.
she's the size of a small horse and she thinks she's a lap dog.
(Chakra leans her entire weight against your leg. This is affection. This is also a takeover.)
(Chakra joined your little crowd! 🖤)
The associate straightens her paper hat. "Hi! What can I get started for you?"
okay. okay okay okay. …a LOT of burgers.
she means it. don't round down.
raw onion. extra cheese. extra spread. on all of them.
Associate, typing, entirely unbothered: "…extra spread on all of them. Got it."
fries animal style. that's not optional, that's structural.
two drinks. and a shake.
…one shake?
one shake. two straws.
(the associate looks up. the associate approves.)
and — this is going to sound strange — could we have two of the hats?
Associate: "Nobody has ever asked me that so politely."
She slides two folded paper hats across the counter, one for each of you.
(you both put them on immediately. neither of you takes them off.)
[TODO Noah: what actually happened the first time we came here ♥]
Red board, white letters, five things on it and not one thing more.
the whole menu fits on one sign and it's still the correct answer every time.
…the prices on this board are from 1976.
it's my pixel restaurant. the double-double is two forty-five and I won't be taking questions.
Whole potatoes going into the slicer at one end, fries coming out under the heat lamp at the other.
they cut them RIGHT THERE. every time this delights me.
every time. I have watched you watch this.
The whole top wall is glass. Longwood, a slice of sky, and the light coming in flat and gold.
…we live here.
we live here.
there are still eleven boxes.
we live here WITH eleven boxes. that's a detail.
(you stand at the window for a while. Neither of you says anything. It's the good kind.)
[TODO Noah: the first night in this apartment ♥]
The tank hums quietly on its stand. Gravel, a castle, a lot of very green plants.
okay so. this started as 'one small fish'.
it is not one small fish.
it's a whole little world. and every time we hit something together, it gets a new one.
(press E again any time to sit in front of the tank ♥)
A shelf of terracotta under the windows. Soil, a trowel, one very earnest watering can.
I want to grow things. Actual things. Tomatoes. Basil.
we are extremely going to grow things.
this is the starter set. water them, pick them, and we'll scale up to the balcony in spring.
(press E again any time to step into the little greenhouse 🌱)
Eleven boxes. One says MUGS. One just says US, in her handwriting.
we'll do them this weekend.
you said that about last weekend.
and I'll say it about next weekend. it's a tradition now.
The TV on the left wall, the grey sofa parked square in front of it, the blanket already crumpled.
we have watched roughly four minutes of anything on this.
we talk through all of it.
yeah. best four minutes of TV I've ever had.
Two gym bags dumped by the door. One of them is still zipped.
Mia's and Brandon's. she came back an hour ago. he's still there.
…should we be going to the gym?
we should. we will. JVUE has a 24 hour gym so we can lock in.
(we both know we probably won't)
The stairs up to the rest of the house. Somebody's shoes are on the third step.
Mia's floor. those are hers — she leaves them exactly there, every time.
and yes, she already likes you more than she likes me. it took about ten minutes.
The oven light is on. Something in there is going gold at the edges.
what is that.
I don't know yet. that's the fun part.
(His mom, without turning around: "Twelve more minutes. Nobody opens it.")
His mom turns around with flour on one cheek and a tray in both hands.
"There she IS." (the tray goes down. you do not.)
Mom: "Sit, sit — no, first, taste this. Then sit."
she's been baking since eight this morning. for four people.
Mom: "There are SIX of us, and that's before Mia goes back for more."
(she pushes a warm one into your hand before you can answer. It's perfect.)
[TODO Noah: what mom actually said about her ♥]
His dad looks up over his glasses, entirely delighted, and does not get up.
Dad: "Ah — you must be the famous Sasha."
hi! it's so good to finally—
Dad: "I hear you're studying international relations."
…I am?
Dad: "Good. Because relations in THIS house are strictly domestic."
(silence. he is thrilled with himself.)
he has been holding that one since Tuesday.
Dad: "Since MONDAY." (he shakes your hand with both of his.)
Dad: "He talks about you constantly, you know. Constantly. It's become a whole thing."
His sister, in black sweats, hair still wet, eating something directly out of the pan.
Mia.
Mia: "So YOU'RE the reason he's been unbearable."
…unbearable?
Mia: "Unbearable. Smiling at his phone. In public." (she hugs you before you can decide whether to hug her.)
wait — where's Brandon?
Mia: "Gym."
…still?
Mia: "Still. He'll text me a picture of the treadmill like it's a postcard."
she left him there. she does this.
Mia: "I did my part. Okay — you're staying for dinner, that's not a question." 🖤
A border collie comes around the corner at roughly the speed of sound.
White, with black over one ear and most of one eye — so he always looks like he's asking a question.
oh he's BEAUTIFUL — what's his name?
…Charlie.
Charlie.
Charlie.
we have two Charlies.
we have two Charlies. nobody planned it. nobody's fixing it.
(Charlie #2 does one lap of the whole room to celebrate.)
(He spots Mookie. He stops. He side-eyes Mookie the entire way past.)
(He decides you are his person now. Charlie joined your little crowd! 🐕)
A pinned world map the length of the wall, red string running between five thumbtacks.
this is the wall. everyone in the program has put a pin in this wall.
which ones are yours?
…all five of these, actually.
of COURSE they are.
international affairs and political science. which mostly means I get very upset about places I've never been.
and then you go to them. that's the part people miss.
(she moves one pin two centimetres to the left. It was bothering her.)
A floor globe on a brass meridian, worn smooth around the equator by ten thousand hands.
(She spins it, closes her eyes, and puts a finger down.)
…the middle of the Pacific Ocean.
booking it.
The co-op board. Six months on, six months off, and every posting on it has its tabs torn off.
two of these were yours.
TJX. marketing. that was the first one.
and you hated it.
I hated it. and I want to be fair — some of that was just the work.
…most of it was the people I was working for.
I remember hearing about it. every day. in detail.
you were very patient.
and then Wellington.
and then WELLINGTON.
I LIKE the people. genuinely. I look forward to going in, which I did not know was a thing that could happen to a person.
they'd keep you, you know.
…they might, actually. part time, through my last year.
which starts after this summer. which is — oh. that's now, isn't it.
a full course load and a job at once.
yes.
you're going to be unbearable about how well it goes ♥
A row of little flags on brass poles, none of them hanging quite level.
One for every language taught on this floor.
I can order coffee wrong in four of these.
that's four more than me.
A six-axis arm on a pedestal, sweeping slowly through the same arc, over and over.
okay. this is the one. this is my favourite object in the building.
He taps something. The arm swings out, closes on a little red cube, lifts it, sets it down half an inch to the left.
it has been doing that since 2019.
…that's it? that's the whole thing?
that's the whole thing. and getting it to do THAT reliably is about nine hundred hours of somebody's life.
(The arm sets the cube down. Perfectly. Again.)
okay it's kind of beautiful.
IT'S KIND OF BEAUTIFUL.
(She makes it wave. It waves. She's delighted.)
Two printers running. Gantries tracking left and right, beds sliding, layers stacking up one at a time.
what are they making?
that one's a bracket. that one is… hm.
(You both lean in. The part on the second bed is unmistakably a small pink heart.)
…somebody's calibrating.
somebody is NOT calibrating.
somebody put that on the queue eleven minutes ago and I refuse to say who.
(It finishes. He pops it off the bed with a spatula while it's still warm and hands it to you.)
(You put it in your pocket. It stays there.)
A tracked rover parked by the wall. There's masking tape on the side with a name on it — crossed out twice.
it's had three names. currently it's 'ROOMBA (LEGALLY DISTINCT)'.
what were the other two?
we don't say the second one out loud in this building.
The bench: an oscilloscope drawing a lazy green line, an iron still warm, and four spools of wire.
I have burned myself on that iron more times than I've burned myself cooking.
you've burned yourself cooking a LOT.
which is what makes the statistic impressive.
A whiteboard nobody has erased since March. Kinematics, a half-rubbed plot, and a doodle of a very angry robot.
In the corner, small, in different handwriting: DO NOT ERASE (SERIOUSLY)
that's mine. and I no longer remember what it was for.
The little two-top by the front window. Two chairs, a round marble top, and the good light.
here.
this table. this exact table.
I came through that door, I was looking at my phone, and I looked up — and you were sitting right there in that chair.
I remember what I was wearing.
I remember EVERYTHING you were wearing. I also remember walking straight past you and then standing at the counter for a full minute deciding whether to turn around.
you turned around.
I turned around.
(You both sit down in the same two chairs. It fits exactly the way it did.)
[TODO Noah: what you actually said when you turned around ♥]
A framed screenshot on the wall in a slightly-too-serious black frame, with a little brass plaque under it.
It's two tiny profile cards side by side, with a heart between them.
…did they frame a dating app.
the plaque says 'THE ALGORITHM: 1, EVERY WELL-MEANING FRIEND WE HAVE: 0'.
we met on HINGE.
we met on Hinge! the app designed to be deleted! and we deleted it! it WORKED!
your first message was about my third photo.
it was a GOOD third photo. I thought about that message for twenty minutes.
it was eleven words.
twenty minutes. eleven words. best return on investment of my entire life.
(Somewhere out there is a server with the exact timestamp on it. Neither of you needs to look it up.)
The counter: tip jar, card reader, a stack of cups, and a barista who has seen you two a lot.
Barista: "The usual? Cortado and the cold brew?"
…yes please.
Barista, already making it: "You always take the window table."
we always take the window table.
A Boston terrier is sitting dead centre of the lab floor like he is chairing the meeting.
…that's Rhett.
does he WORK here?
he has a badge. I have seen the badge.
(Rhett accepts exactly one head scratch, then leans his entire body weight against your shins.)
he only does that to people he's already decided about ♥
A husky is asleep under the co-op board with all four legs in the air.
PAWS.
(Paws does not open his eyes. …Paws opens one eye.)
he's the mascot. he's technically staff.
he's technically unconscious.
(He gets up, shakes out, and falls in behind you like it was always the plan.)

greet_la.text: hey you. welcome to Mini-LA — I shrunk my hometown so you'd finally visit.
see those sparkles? each one is something I remember. go poke them. I'll come with you.
(and keep an eye out for figs. you'll know why.)

chat.text: the sparkles are memories. the figs are figs. the cat is a menace.
there's a road east of here. it leads somewhere that smells like Greece.
I hid figs in the tall grass. Mookie may or may not have moved some.
[TODO Noah: add more small talk lines — these cycle when she talks to you.]

lines: (Mookie headbutts your ankle, then acts like it never happened.)
Mookie: meow. meow meow. (a full speech. no notes.)
(Mookie is following you. He would follow you anywhere.)

leo.text: (Leo flops over sideways with total confidence that someone will catch him.)
(Leo and Mookie exchange a long look. Diplomacy is ongoing.)

charlie.text: (Charlie's whole back half is wagging. All of it.)
(Charlie tries to herd the cats. It is not going well. He is undeterred.)

chakra.text: (Chakra sits on your foot. Both of your feet. It's fine, you didn't need those.)
(that was the deepest sound anyone has ever made.)
(Charlie has been trying to get Chakra to play for ten minutes. She has blinked once.)
(Chakra checks over her shoulder every few steps to make sure you're still there. 🖤)

collie.text: (Charlie — the collie one — has already run the length of the street twice.)
(He is back. He is somehow not tired.)
(He drops a stick at your feet. You did not throw a stick. He found a stick.)
(Charlie is very carefully herding the entire group into a tighter shape.)
(Nobody agreed to this. It is working anyway.)
(Charlie glances at Mookie. Mookie does not glance back.)
(Charlie decides to walk on the far side of you. Just in case. 👀)
(Two Charlies. You call one name and get two heads.)
we've fully accepted it. they answer as a unit now.
(one eye is black, one eye is white, both eyes are locked on you.)

kitten.text: (the kitten is asleep on your foot. you are not going anywhere.)
(the kitten attacks your shoelace, misses entirely, and walks away as if that was the plan.)
(Mookie is watching from a shelf. the truce is holding. barely.)

rhett.text: (Rhett is sitting on your foot. this is a Boston terrier's love language.)
(he sneezes. it is the loudest thing that has ever happened in this building.)
(Rhett looks up at Chakra. Chakra could eat him. they are best friends.)

paws.text: (Paws leans on you until you are structurally involved.)
(he says something. it isn't a bark, it's a whole sentence, and it's an argument.)
(Paws has decided the front of the group is his. nobody is contesting it.)

la_neighbor.text: Lovely couple. You two remind me of me and my wife.
Now shoo — you're standing on my sprinklers.
Back again? The shaved ice place down the street is the real landmark.

care_aide.text: "You're the granddaughter! She talks about you constantly. CONSTANTLY."
"…and about a tall young man. Is that him? Hm. She undersold him, actually."
"If she offers you food, take the food. It is not really an offer."
"She did her hair herself this morning. She knew you were coming ♥"

route_hiker.text: Careful up ahead — someone on a quad bike went by screaming about figs.

route_admirer.text: (she squints at the pyramid, counting on her fingers)
Greece, Italy, Egypt, Mexico, Moldova… all that together? I can't even commit to a coffee order.
One little road, a whole world on it. You two collect countries like I collect parking tickets.

bos_student.text: Is that a cat following you? Lucky. Mine won't even look at me.

bos_runner.text: Go Terriers! …or Huskies. I forget which school I go to.

bos_oldman.text: The Charles is lovely this time of year. Don't drink it, though.

bos_neighbor.text: You're the one from downstairs' boy's girl, aren't you.
…that came out wrong. Anyway. Welcome to Brookline.
Trash goes out Tuesday. Somebody had to tell you.

io_cook.text: He turns a basket of fries without looking up.
"Animal style takes an extra minute. It's worth the extra minute."

io_cashier.text: "Take your time. The board hasn't changed since 1948."

io_customer.text: A man is halfway through a double-double and will not be interrupted.
He raises the burger a few inches. That's the whole greeting.

neu_prof.text: She looks up from a stack of position papers, glasses pushed into her hair.
"Ah — one of mine. Good. Tell me you finished the Moldova brief."
(You did. You finished it four days early. She already knows.)
"The trick isn't having an opinion. Everyone has an opinion."
"The trick is being able to argue the other side well enough that it hurts."

neu_husky.text: "Do you know if the spring co-op postings are up yet?"
"…they're not up yet. I've checked eleven times. I'm going to check again."
"Six months in class, six months at a desk, forever. It's a beautiful system."
"I have no idea what month it is."

bu_grad.text: A grad student surfaces from behind a monitor, holding a screwdriver like a pen.
"Oh — hey. Don't touch the arm." (a pause) "…okay, touch the arm. It's fine. It's rated for it."
"Print's at ninety-four percent. It'll fail at ninety-six. It always fails at ninety-six."
"I've stopped being sad about it. Now it's just a thing that happens, like weather."
"You're the one from the photo on his desk."
(you didn't know there was a photo on his desk.)

cafe_barista.text: "Window table's free." (she says it before either of you asks.)
"It's always free when you two come in. I don't make the rules."
"You know you ordered the exact same thing the first time you sat there."
"I remember because he ordered wrong twice."

cafe_regular.text: An older man with a newspaper he is not reading.
"Me too. Forty-one years with mine. Same booth. Keep the table."

all.text: unstoppable. the strangers' trees of Greece never stood a chance.
(that's every pumpkin. all of them. the entire harvest.)
you collected all the pumpkins! for what reason? PUMPKINN!!
there's no prize. I want to be really clear that there was never going to be a prize.
